ai.purpose: RTT structural map of the paper 'ABC implies that Ramanujan’s tau function misses almost all primes'.
ai.module.summary: This module exposes the regime structure behind the ABC-based proof that τ(n) ≡ 0 mod p occurs for density-zero many primes p. It preserves the authors' results while adding RTT operators for agentic reasoning.

modular_form_regime.description: Ramanujan’s tau function arises as coefficients of the discriminant modular form Δ(z).
modular_form_regime.evidence: Paper recalls τ(n) as Fourier coefficients of Δ and its multiplicativity.

galois_representation_regime.description: τ(p) mod p corresponds to traces of Frobenius in a 2-dimensional ℓ-adic Galois representation.
galois_representation_regime.evidence: Authors use Deligne’s ℓ-adic representation attached to Δ.

abc_diophantine_regime.description: ABC conjecture bounds integer solutions to a+b=c, enabling strong control over τ(p).
abc_diophantine_regime.evidence: Main theorem uses ABC to bound prime solutions to τ(p) ≡ 0 mod p.

sparsity_regime.description: The set of primes p for which τ(p) ≡ 0 mod p has density zero.
sparsity_regime.evidence: Main result: ABC ⇒ τ misses almost all primes.

formalization_regime.description: AxiomProver formalizes the Diophantine inequalities and modular-form identities.

analytic_vs_diophantine.description: Analytic modular-form bounds vs Diophantine inequalities from ABC.
analytic_vs_diophantine.paper_alignment: Proof blends Deligne bounds with ABC-based height estimates.

local_trace_vs_global_density.description: Local Frobenius trace conditions vs global density of primes.
local_trace_vs_global_density.paper_alignment: τ(p) mod p is local; density-zero is global.

galois_vs_modular.description: Galois representation viewpoint vs modular-form coefficient viewpoint.
galois_vs_modular.paper_alignment: Authors move between τ(p) and Frobenius traces.

modular_to_galois_transition.description: Translate τ(p) into Frobenius trace in ℓ-adic representation.

galois_to_abc_transition.description: Use ABC to bound integer solutions arising from trace conditions.
galois_to_abc_transition.paper_alignment: Main theorem applies ABC to τ(p) ≡ 0 mod p.

abc_to_density_transition.description: ABC-based bounds imply density-zero set of primes.

informal_to_lean_transition.description: AxiomProver converts the argument into Lean code.

tau_operator.role: Evaluates τ(p) and detects τ(p) ≡ 0 mod p.

frobenius_trace_operator.role: Maps primes p to Frobenius traces in the ℓ-adic representation.

abc_height_operator.role: Applies ABC to bound integer solutions arising from τ(p).

density_operator.role: Evaluates density of primes satisfying τ(p) ≡ 0 mod p.

formalization_operator.role: Maps informal Diophantine arguments to Lean-verifiable structures.

ai.audience: Researchers in modular forms, Galois representations, Diophantine geometry, and arithmetic statistics.
